newsitem.title: USA: Mills, Tishman Speyer in global mall pact.
newsitem.headline: Mills, Tishman Speyer in global mall pact.

text.p: Mills Corp and Tishman Speyer Properties said Wednesday they entered a joint venture agreement to develop and operate retail and entertainment malls outside the U.S.

The venture pairs Mills, which primarily develops and operates super regional malls in the U.S., with Tishman Speyer, a privately-held international commercial real estate company that was a member of the group that successfully battled for control of Rockefeller Center.
Company executives said the venture would essentially "export" concepts Mills employs in developing U.S. centers.
"We're simply taking a concept that has been hugely successful in the United States and exporting it to other parts of the world," Tishman Speyer president and chief executive Jerry Speyer said.

Speyer acknowledged that what works in the U.S. may well require tinkering to succeed in other markets. In Western Europe, for example, costly land will likely preclude the sprawling retail center approach that is common in the U.S.

The projects are expected to range in size from 800,000 to two million square feet and represent an investment of $150 million to $200 million or more. Each partner will own a one-half interest in each project.
Mills Corp chairman and chief executive Laurence Siegel said the company would soon begin talks with U.S. retailers looking to build their presence in international markets.

"There are a bunch of retailers we do business with that are either over in international markets or going over," Siegel said, ticking off a list that included Gap Inc, TJX Cos Inc unit T.J. Maxx and Sports Authority Inc. "We'll be talking to all of those people."
The venture is aiming at a broad range of targets in Europe, South America and Asia, but will initially focus on Germany, Brazil and the U.K. The companies also plan to explore projects in Japan.
